title: Turn on lost-phone settings before you need them
summary: Find My iPhone, Google Find Hub and Samsung Find have critical tracking settings to enable now, before your phone ever goes missing or stolen.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You know that awful feeling when you reach for your phone, and it is suddenly nowhere to be found. Maybe you left it at a restaurant. Maybe it slipped between the car seats. Or maybe somebody walked away with it. The worst time to start figuring out your phone's tracking features is after it disappears. Fortunately, iPhone, Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones include powerful tools that can help you locate a missing device and protect the information stored on it. Take a few minutes while your phone is still safely in your hand and make sure these settings are ready.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT
Turn on your phone’s lost-device and theft protections now, so you are ready to locate it and protect your data if it disappears. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
Turn on Find My iPhone in iOS 27

Apple's Find My system can help locate an iPhone when it is online. With the right settings enabled, supported iPhones can also remain findable when they are offline or for a period after they have been turned off.
Open SettingsTap your nameTap Find MyTap Find My iPhoneTurn on Find My iPhoneTurn on Find My networkTurn on Send Last Location
Open Settings
Tap your name
Tap Find My
Tap Find My iPhone
Turn on Find My iPhone
Turn on Find My network
Turn on Send Last Location

Find My network lets nearby Apple devices securely help locate your iPhone when it cannot connect to Wi-Fi or cellular service. On supported iPhones, Apple says the Find My network can locate the phone for up to 24 hours after it is turned off or up to five hours while it is in power reserve mode. Meanwhile, Send Last Location automatically sends your iPhone's location to Apple when its battery reaches a critically low level. That could give you one more place to check if the battery dies before you realize your phone is missing.

While you are there, I would check another iPhone security feature called Stolen Device Protection. Open Settings > Face ID & Passcode and enter your passcode. Tap Stolen Device Protection, then make sure it is turned on. By default, Apple applies its added security requirements when your iPhone is away from familiar locations such as home or work. You can make those protections stronger by choosing Always under Require Security Delay. Stolen Device Protection can require Face ID or Touch ID for sensitive actions. Certain account changes can also trigger a one-hour Security Delay followed by another biometric check. Find My cannot be turned off while Stolen Device Protection is enabled. That extra hurdle can be especially useful if someone steals your iPhone and has also seen or learned your passcode.
STOLEN IPHONES FUEL SCARY PASSCODE SCAM
iPhone owners can use Apple’s Find My network to help locate a missing device even when it goes offline. (Apple)
Google Pixel owners should check Find Hub

Google now calls its lost-device service Find Hub. If you have added a Google Account to your Pixel, Find Hub is usually enabled automatically. Still, I would check these settings before you ever need them.
Open SettingsTap Security & privacyTap Lost device protectionTap Find HubMake sure Allow device to be located is turned onTap Find your offline devicesChoose the offline-finding option you prefer
Open Settings
Tap Security & privacy
Tap Lost device protection
Tap Find Hub
Make sure Allow device to be located is turned on
Tap Find your offline devices
Choose the offline-finding option you prefer
For the broadest coverage, choose With network everywhere if that option appears on your Pixel. This lets nearby Android devices help locate your phone when it cannot connect normally.

You should also open Settings > Location and make sure Use location is turned on. Google recommends setting a PIN, pattern or password too. A screen lock helps your Pixel use Find Hub's end-to-end encrypted offline-finding network. Supported newer Pixel phones can also remain findable through Find Hub for several hours after the battery runs out or the phone is powered off. For that feature to work, Bluetooth, Location and offline finding should be enabled before the phone shuts down.

Go to Settings > Security & privacy > Lost device protection. From there, review the additional theft safeguards available on your Pixel. Depending on your device and software version, you may see Theft Detection Lock, Offline Device Lock, Remote Lock and Identity Check. These features can automatically lock your phone in certain situations or require biometric authentication before sensitive account changes are made. Find Hub helps you locate the phone, while these additional protections can help secure it if someone takes it.
Pixel owners can use Google Find Hub and offline finding to help track down a phone when it loses its normal connection. (Google)
Samsung Galaxy owners have two finding systems
If you use a Samsung Galaxy phone, you can take advantage of both Google Find Hub and Samsung's own device-finding tools.
Open SettingsTap Security and privacyTap Lost device protectionTap Find My MobileTurn on Allow this phone to be foundTurn on Send last locationTurn on Offline finding
Open Settings
Tap Security and privacy
Tap Lost device protection
Tap Find My Mobile
Turn on Allow this phone to be found
Turn on Send last location
Turn on Offline finding

You will need a Samsung account on the phone to use Samsung Find and SmartThings Find. Send last location can preserve the phone's last known location. Offline finding lets nearby Galaxy devices help update the location when your phone cannot connect normally. Samsung says that if the phone is powered off, you may only see its last known location. That makes turning these protections on ahead of time especially useful.

I would keep Google Find Hub available on a Samsung phone as well. Samsung's current instructions say you can verify it by opening Settings > Google Services > Find Hub > tap on your device > Settings and checking that Allow device to be located is turned on. That gives Galaxy owners another way to locate or secure a missing phone through their Google Account. You may see slightly different wording depending on your Galaxy model, carrier or software version. Samsung notes that some menus can vary between devices.
Galaxy owners can use Samsung Find alongside Google Find Hub to help locate and secure a missing phone. (Samsung)
What to do when your phone actually disappears
If an iPhone goes missing, open Find My on another Apple device or use Apple's Find Devices service through iCloud.com. From there, you can view the phone on a map, play a sound or mark it as lost.

Google Pixel and other Android owners can open the Find Hub app on another Android device or use Google's Find Hub through a web browser. You can locate the phone, play a sound or mark it as lost. You can also erase the device remotely if recovery looks unlikely.
Samsung Galaxy owners can use Samsung Find or SmartThings Find through their Samsung account in addition to Google Find Hub.

If the phone appears to be sitting somewhere nearby, playing a sound can save you from tearing the house apart. However, if the map shows your phone somewhere unfamiliar and you suspect it was stolen, avoid trying to recover it yourself. Contact law enforcement instead.
Watch out for scams after your phone is stolen

Losing the phone can also open the door to another problem. Thieves have used convincing Apple-style texts and fake Find My websites to trick stolen iPhone owners into revealing their passcodes. A message may claim that your missing phone has suddenly been found and include a link where you can supposedly see its location. Avoid tapping those links. Instead, open Find My yourself or go directly to Apple's official Find Devices service. The same basic rule applies to Android. If a message claims your missing device has been located, open Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly rather than signing in through a link somebody sent you.

Pro tip: Use strong antivirus software. Strong security software can help warn you about malicious links, phishing sites and other online threats that may appear after your phone is stolen. It adds another layer of protection, but you should still avoid clicking unexpected messages claiming your missing phone has been found. Instead, open Find My, Google Find Hub or Samsung Find directly. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
A few minutes now can save a lot of panic later

Most of us do not think much about these settings while our phone is sitting safely in our hand. Then the phone disappears and suddenly every one of them becomes very important. I would check them now. Make sure your phone can be located, make sure offline finding is enabled and confirm that you know which account you would need to sign in to from another device. You may never need any of these features. If you do, you will already know where to start.
Kurt's key takeaways

Your phone already has some impressive tools for finding it, but those tools work best when you prepare before the phone goes missing. On an iPhone, I would make sure Find My network and Send Last Location are enabled. Pixel owners should check Find Hub and offline finding, while Galaxy users can add Samsung's Lost device protection on top of Google's system. I would also spend another minute reviewing the theft protections available on your phone. Apple's Stolen Device Protection and Google's theft protection features can make it harder for someone who gets your phone to take control of your accounts. That extra layer could become incredibly valuable when you are already dealing with the stress of a missing device.
If your phone disappeared right now, would you know exactly how to find and protect it, or would you be learning these settings for the first time? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Luxury fashion designers found shot dead in California as family reportedly reveals troubling lead-up
summary: Fashion designers Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found shot dead outside their California home as relatives reportedly revealed troubling details about the days before their deaths.
story: Aerial video shows police at the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2. Credit: KTVU
The husband and wife behind a California luxury clothing brand were found shot dead outside their hillside home, as relatives reportedly revealed troubling details about the days before their deaths.

Oakland police confirmed to Fox News Digital that Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were the two people found dead on Oct. 2 in the 400 block of Panoramic Way. The couple founded women’s luxury apparel company Bryn Walker.
Min’s brother, Paul Min, told the Los Angeles Times he believes Walker fatally shot his sister before turning the gun on himself. Police have not confirmed that account.
"This remains an active and ongoing investigation. No additional details are being provided at this time," Oakland police told Fox News Digital.
KANSAS CONVICTED FELON, SEX OFFENDER ALLEGEDLY KILLS FELLOW FAMILY MEMBERS BEFORE TAKING HIS OWN LIFE: POLICE
Police vehicles outside the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
A bouquet and handwritten closure notice appear outside a Bryn Walker storefront after the luxury clothing brand’s founders were found dead outside their Oakland home. (KTVU)
Paul Min described a troubling decline in his brother-in-law after he allegedly lost millions of dollars in risky financial ventures, according to the outlet.

He called Walker the "most honest, responsible, hardworking guy you have ever known" and struggled to reconcile the suspected violence with the man he had known and loved for nearly four decades, the outlet reported.
TIKTOK INFLUENCER WHO ACCUSED ESTRANGED HUSBAND OF PEDOPHILIA FOUND DEAD IN POSSIBLE MURDER-SUICIDE
An aerial view of the Panoramic Hill neighborhood, where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead outside their home Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Min said he and his sister agreed Walker needed psychiatric help after Walker allegedly suggested that the three of them "end things."
Michelle Min was planning to have her husband admitted for psychiatric treatment on the day of the shooting, her brother told the outlet.
‘MARVELOUS MRS. MAISEL’ SET DECORATOR SLAIN, HUSBAND FOUND DEAD IN FAMILY ALREADY SCARRED BY HOME KILLING
A police officer handles yellow tape near the scene where Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead in Oakland on Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Police have not confirmed the family’s claims about Walker’s mental health, financial losses or a possible motive.

Berkeley officers responded to Panoramic Way shortly after 10:30 a.m. Friday and found a man and woman suffering from gunshot wounds, KTLA reported. Officers attempted lifesaving measures until paramedics arrived, but the couple was pronounced dead at the scene.
Oakland police, the lead investigating agency, recovered a gun and had not ruled out murder-suicide or determined who fired the weapon, the Los Angeles Times reported.
FATHER-IN-LAW OF TRANS NYT EXEC ADMITTED KILLING HIM, WORKED 'IN CONCERT' WITH MOTHER-IN-LAW: DOCS
A Bryn Walker storefront in Berkeley, California. The brand’s founders, Bryan Walker and Michelle Min, were found dead outside their Oakland home Oct. 2, 2026. (Google Maps)
The couple met in Kansas in the 1980s before following Min’s parents to California and eventually building their Berkeley clothing business, according to the LA Times.

Bryn Walker has been based in Berkeley since 1992 and designs and produces its clothing in the San Francisco Bay Area, according to the company’s website. The brand says it operates six company-owned stores and supplies roughly 1,000 boutiques nationwide.
Its store directory lists two Berkeley locations and a shop in Vineyard Haven, Massachusetts, on Martha’s Vineyard.
Police gather outside the Oakland home where Bryn Walker founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min were found dead Oct. 2, 2026. (KTVU)
Fox News Digital also reached out to Berkeley police for comment.

title: Convicted child predator allegedly attacks two women inside Planet Fitness women's locker room
summary: A convicted child rapist allegedly attacked a woman at a Planet Fitness before sexually assaulting an employee who intervened. He is being held without bail.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A convicted child rapist allegedly attacked a woman after bringing her to a Planet Fitness gym to use the showers, then allegedly sexually assaulted an employee who tried to intervene.

Laquan Holland, 40, allegedly beat the woman, tried to strip off her clothing and blocked her escape inside the Cambridge, Massachusetts, gym, the Middlesex District Attorney’s Office told Fox News Digital.
The attack came weeks after a charge accusing Holland of failing to register as a sex offender was dismissed on the condition that he complete his registration, prosecutors confirmed.
Holland was ordered held without bail after his arraignment on two counts of assault to rape, two counts of indecent assault and battery, kidnapping and witness intimidation.
MICHIGAN DECISION FORCES REMOVAL OF DISGRACED SPORTS DOCTOR LARRY NASSAR FROM SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY
Laquan Holland, 40, is accused of sexually assaulting two women inside the women’s locker room at this Planet Fitness in Cambridge’s Porter Square on Oct. 1, 2026. (Google Maps)
A dangerousness hearing is scheduled for Oct. 16. NBC10 Boston reported that a not guilty plea was entered on his behalf.
Prosecutors said Holland, a member of the Porter Square gym, arrived around 9 a.m. Oct. 1 with a woman he knew after offering to let her use the showers.
But once they arrived, Holland allegedly began hitting her.
CALIFORNIA DEMS TRIGGER OUTRAGE AFTER SIDING WITH CONVICTED CHILD SEX OFFENDERS IN SHOCKING VOTE

The woman fled into the women’s locker room and shower area, authorities said. Holland allegedly followed, continuing to hit and touch her inappropriately while trying to remove her clothing and preventing her from leaving, according to the DA’s office.
WASHINGTON MOTHER SAYS SHE FOUND ADULT MALE SHOWERING IN WOMEN'S LOCKER ROOM DURING CHILDREN'S SWIM MEET
A convicted child rapist allegedly attacked a woman at a Planet Fitness before sexually assaulting an employee who intervened. (Don Emmert/AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images)
A female employee entered the shower area and tried to pull Holland off the woman. He allegedly sexually assaulted her, too.
Police arrived to find Holland in the locker room trying to put his clothes back on, prosecutors said.
Holland’s criminal history includes guilty pleas in 2006 to two counts of child rape and one count of indecent assault and battery on a child under 14, Boston.com reported, citing court records.
REPEAT OFFENDER WITH 7 PRIOR CONVICTIONS ARRESTED 3 TIMES IN 12 DAYS OVER ALLEGED ATTACKS ON WOMEN
The suspect was held without bail after prosecutors said he attacked two women inside a Planet Fitness locker room. (Andrew H. Walker/Getty Images for Planet Fitness)
More recently, Cambridge police arrested him Aug. 25 for failing to register as a sex offender, a subsequent offense, according to police records reviewed by Fox News Digital.
The DA’s office said Holland, who is homeless and was known to stay in Cambridge and Boston, must complete registration and verification requirements every 30 days.

He showed up at Cambridge police headquarters to register Aug. 25 but was arrested because he was late, prosecutors said. The charge was later dismissed on the condition that he register, which he completed Aug. 27.
FEMALE VIRGINIA OFFICER SUES POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHARING LOCKER ROOM WITH BIOLOGICAL MALE
Planet Fitness told Fox News Digital that the franchise operator canceled Holland’s membership and is cooperating with investigators.

"Planet Fitness is committed to providing a safe environment for all. The franchise group has cancelled the membership of the individual involved and is working with local law enforcement to support their investigation into this matter," the company said.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Christa Pike execution failure spares murderer who bailed victim out just to kill him
summary: Gary Wayne Sutton's Dec. 3 execution is on hold after Tennessee's botched lethal injection of Christa Pike prompted Gov. Bill Lee to halt deaths.
story: Botched lethal injection attempts leave Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike in critical condition, prompting the resignation of the state's prison chief. Gov. Bill Lee postpones all executions through 2026 as an independent review begins. UC Berkeley Law professor John Yoo analyzes the legal controversy and previews key cases as the Supreme Court prepares to kick off its new term.

The execution of a double murderer who bailed one of his victims out of jail only for the man to be shot dead — and then killed his sister when she went looking for him — has been put on hold after Tennessee's botched attempt to lethally inject Christa Pike for her role in the "satanic" torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995.
Gov. Bill Lee halted the death penalty across the state for the rest of the year — but there was only one scheduled, the Dec. 3 execution of convicted double murderer Gary Wayne Sutton.
His uncle and co-defendant, James Dellinger, died of natural causes on death row in 2023.
FORMER KNOXVILLE POLICE CHIEF SAYS INVESTIGATORS ARE STILL HAUNTED BY COLLEEN SLEMMER'S MURDER 31 YEARS LATER
Gary Wayne Sutton pictured in a mugshot taken on Nov. 11, 2025, at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Tennessee. (Tennessee Department of Correction)
Sutton has maintained his innocence — but in separate trials, he was convicted in the murders of Tommy Griffin and Connie Branam, a brother and sister who were killed on Feb. 21 and 22, 1992.

Sutton, who months earlier had beaten up Griffin's brother, went drinking with Dellinger and Griffin at a bar called Howie's Hideaway on Feb. 21, 1992, according to court records reviewed by Fox News Digital.
After they left, they got in a fight, and Sutton and Dellinger left Griffin on the roadside. He encountered a passing driver who flagged down a police officer, according to court documents.
CHRISTA PIKE'S BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTION TAKES FOCUS OFF VICTIM, JEOPARDIZES EXECUTION: FORMER POLICE CHIEF
Christa Gail Pike appears remotely from Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation for her hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tenn., on Aug. 11, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The responding officer reported that Griffin was "on the verge of tears" and shirtless with "scrapes and scratches" on his upper body and a cut behind his ear. Griffin claimed he had gotten into "an argument with some friends, who were not really his friends," according to court records.

title: 'American Idol' alum Caleb Flynn weeps as daughters ask him why he killed their mother, vow not to visit him
summary: Caleb Flynn was sentenced to life without parole, plus 16 years, after an Ohio jury convicted the former "American Idol" contestant of murdering his wife.
story: Caleb Flynn addresses his daughters before he is sentenced for murdering their mother.

Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn was sentenced Monday to life without the possibility of parole for murdering his wife, with an Ohio judge ordering him to first serve 16 additional years behind bars.

Miami County Judge Jeannine N. Pratt ordered Flynn to serve seven years for firearm specifications followed by nine years for three counts of tampering with evidence before beginning his life sentence for the murder of Ashley Flynn.

Pratt said consecutive sentences were necessary to protect the public and punish Flynn, finding the harm caused by his crimes was so severe that a single prison term would not adequately reflect the seriousness of his conduct.
'AMERICAN IDOL' ALUM CALEB FLYNN CONVICTED OF MURDERING HIS WIFE
Before Flynn was sentenced, one of his daughters confronted him in a letter read aloud in court by her uncle, Matthew Keyt.
Caleb Flynn stands in court, Sept. 29, as an Ohio jury returns guilty verdicts on all nine charges in the murder of his wife, Ashley Flynn. (Credit: WKEF)

"How could you do such a thing? I looked up to you. I loved you with all my heart," Flynn's daughter wrote. "Mommy was the perfect person. The absolute perfect person. What did she ever do to make you hate her so much?"
She wrote that she cries every day over her mother's death but still prays every night for her father to confess and repent.
"It was your choice to have an affair. It was your choice to lie to everyone," she wrote. "It was your choice to leave your only two daughters."
CALEB FLYNN'S LOVE SONGS TO MISTRESS PLAYED IN COURT AS RELATIVES AWKWARDLY LOOK ON
Flynn's other daughter also confronted her father in a letter read aloud by her grandmother, Jill Smith.
"The least you could do is tell everyone you did it and receive your outcome," she wrote. "Also, please repent to God, the one who created you. Your time isn't over."
WATCH: Letter from Caleb Flynn's daughter read in court before sentencing
She questioned how her father could stand in church and sing about his love for God while keeping secrets from his family, and told him Ashley was "the best thing that ever happened to you."
"Through all of what you put me through, God is going to work something out for good," she wrote. "And by the way, I don't plan on coming to see you."
As his daughter's words were read aloud, Flynn could be heard sobbing into a tissue at the defense table.
Ashley's sister, Kayla Keyt, also addressed Flynn directly, telling him he had taken a mother from her daughters and shattered a family that trusted him.
DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER
Caleb Flynn cries in court as a statement is read from one of his daughters before he was sentenced to life without the chance of parole, for killing his wife Ashley Flynn. (WKEF)
"You took Ashley from the earth," Keyt said. "You took a mother from her daughters."
Keyt told Flynn she nevertheless forgave him, saying she refused to allow hatred and bitterness to take anything else from her family.
WATCH: Ashley Flynn's sister rips her killer Caleb Flynn

Flynn addressed the court before sentencing, saying it was his first opportunity to speak publicly in eight months. He first addressed his daughters, telling them they remained his "greatest joy" and apologizing for the milestones he would miss.
Flynn later apologized to Ashley's family for breaking his marriage vows and for the pain caused by his decisions, saying he took responsibility for his words and actions.
Ashley Flynn's sister, Kayla Keyt, tells Caleb Flynn it was his choice to have an affair and lie to everyone, just before he was sentenced to life behind bars on Oct. 5, 2026. (WKEF)
But he stopped short of accepting responsibility for Ashley's murder.
"I did not kill my wife," Flynn said, adding that he would continue fighting to prove his innocence.
Flynn received credit for 229 days already spent in jail and was ordered to pay $20,000 in restitution for funeral expenses, along with court costs.
Jurors found Flynn guilty of aggravated murder, three counts of murder, two counts of felonious assault and three counts of tampering with evidence after roughly 2½ hours of deliberations.
His defense argued that Flynn has no prior criminal history and is capable of rehabilitation, pointing to his years working in ministry and letters of support from his family.
Flynn's parents were among several relatives who wrote to Pratt asking for mercy ahead of sentencing.

His father, Mike Flynn, told the judge his son's "brokenness, shame, and remorse" were genuine, while his mother, Kim Flynn, wrote that her son had "repented to his Lord" and was remorseful for his decisions. Both asked Pratt for mercy.
Prosecutors sharply disputed that portrayal, arguing Flynn has never accepted responsibility or shown genuine remorse. They are asking Pratt to sentence him to life without the possibility of parole.

The verdict capped a trial that exposed Flynn's secret affair, thousands of messages with his mistress and exchanges about wanting his wife dead before she was shot twice in the back of the head inside the couple's Tipp City home Feb. 16.
Substitute teacher and volleyball coach Ashley Flynn was discovered dead in her Ohio home. Her husband was convicted of her murder. (Ashley Flynn/Facebook; Tipp City Schools)
Prosecutors argued Flynn killed Ashley before staging the scene to make it appear an intruder had broken into the home.
Flynn's affair with Alleigha Botner became a key part of the case. Investigators recovered roughly 107,000 messages between the two, with prosecutors highlighting some of those exchanges for jurors.

Jurors saw messages in which Flynn discussed wanting his wife dead and contemplated ways she could be killed without him going to prison.

Alleigha Botner testifies in the Ohio murder trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn. Prosecutors say Botner had an affair with Flynn before his wife, Ashley Flynn, was killed. (WKEF)

Botner also read messages exchanged in the hours before Ashley's death, including Flynn telling her, "It's happening" and "Tomorrow it all starts." In another exchange, Botner told Flynn, "You're about to be free."

Flynn's defense argued the messages were being taken out of context and that references to being "free" meant divorce rather than murder.

title: Florida student killed in rollover school bus crash
summary: A 10th grade Winter Haven High School student was among two killed in the Polk County school bus crash that injured several others Monday morning.
story: Two people were killed, and multiple others were injured in a multi-vehicle crash involving a school bus in Florida on Monday.
Two people died, including a high school student, and several others suffered injuries after a Florida school bus was struck in a multi-vehicle crash in Polk County on Monday morning.

The crash involved the school bus and three other vehicles, sending multiple people to nearby hospitals. As of a news conference on Monday, authorities confirmed the two deaths and said one person remained in critical condition.
Police have not identified the tenth grade Winter Haven High School student who died in the crash. The other deceased person was inside a silver Jeep that collided with the school bus.
SUPPORTERS OF ALABAMA SCHOOL BUS DRIVER CHARGED IN DEADLY ACCIDENT SAY SHE SUFFERED FROM 'MEDICAL CRISIS'
Authorities in Polk County, Florida, respond to a fatal crash involving a school bus on Monday, October 5, 2026. (WTVT)

Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said the accident occurred at roughly 6:15 a.m. on a two-lane road when a white Chevy Malibu crossed the lane divide into oncoming traffic and struck the rear wheels of the school bus, ripping off one of its tires.
The bus then itself lurched into oncoming traffic, where it collided head-on with the Jeep.
THREE SCHOOL SAFETY STEPS EVERY PARENT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE CLASSES BEGIN
"It was a horrible crash," Judd said during a news conference. "It was a terrible, tragic morning. We had a beautiful 10th grade girl lose her life."
Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd holds a press conference after a fatal crash involving a school bus on October 5, 2026. (WTVT)
The bus was carrying 37 students at the time of the crash, as well as the bus driver and the driver's 9-year-old daughter, police said.

Judd said between five and seven people were transferred to local hospitals with "trauma alerts," and just one was in critical condition. Judd said the injured were brought to hospitals via a combination of helicopters, ambulances and private vehicles.

Authorities say the driver of the Chevy Malibu is cooperating with investigators. The individual, who told police they were on their way to work, has not been arrested.

title: Cornell campus police made drug arrest at Chi Phi fraternity house hours before alleged gang rape
summary: Cornell University campus police made a drug arrest at the Chi Phi fraternity house less than 24 hours before an alleged gang rape at a party there.
story: Fox News correspondent CB Cotton reports on Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff announcing an outside law firm will investigate the school’s response to an alleged 2024 fraternity gang rape on ‘Fox Report.’

Campus police at Cornell University in New York made a drug arrest at the embattled Chi Phi fraternity house on campus less than 24 hours before seven former members are accused in a new civil lawsuit of gang raping a female classmate, according to the school's crime blotter.
The Cornell Daily Sun, an independent campus newspaper at the Ivy League school, resurfaced the daily crime log entry in a new report over the weekend.

Campus police responded to the university-owned frat house around 1 a.m. on Oct. 19, 2024, and arrested a student on drug charges, according to the blotter. It does not include specific charges and indicates that "an individual has been referred to the Office of Student Conduct."
CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS

Police officers respond to an act of vandalism at Day Hall on the campus of Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, Monday, October 5, 2026. The building was vandalized early Monday morning with graffiti amid fallout over the school's response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024. (Everett Chambala / The Cornell Daily Sun)

The blotter does not include details about what type of drug or drugs were involved or whether the arrested individual was a member of Chi Phi. Nor was it immediately clear how the incident was resolved.
Fox News Digital reached out to Cornell for comment and did not immediately receive a response.
CONVICTED RAPIST WHO PREYED ON WOMEN AT AMERICA'S TOP PARTY SCHOOL FACES RECKONING AFTER COURTHOUSE DASH
The fraternity went on to host a party later that day, which stretched into the following morning.
The Chi Phi fraternity house stands on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, N.Y., on Oct. 2, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

That party is identified in the civil lawsuit filed on behalf of an unidentified Jane Doe, who reported allegations of sexual assault to university police on Nov. 8, telling investigators that she was attacked between 11 p.m. on Oct. 19 and 5:45 a.m. on Oct. 20.
PENN STATE FRAT COCAINE BUST BLOWS LID OFF WIDER STIMULANT SCOURGE HITTING COLLEGE CAMPUSES — AND BEYOND
In Doe's lawsuit, she also alleges she had been pressured into snorting ketamine.

Ketamine is an anesthetic with dissociative and hallucinogenic effects, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, which also warns that the drug "has also been used to facilitate sexual assault."
THE FRAT OMERTÀ: WHISTLEBLOWER WARNS OF ‘CODE OF SILENCE’ AFTER OLE MISS DEATHS, ALLEGED PENN STATE COKE RING
A sign on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, New York. (TW Farlow/Getty Images)
The fraternity would later be suspended on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day Doe reported sex assault allegations to campus police, according to Doe's civil complaint.
Separately, vandals smashed windows and painted slogans in red at Day Hall, an administrative building, early Monday, according to images published by the Daily Sun.
STUDENTS AT TOP PARTY COLLEGE ON EDGE AFTER RAPE, STRANGULATION REPORTED IN CAMPUS HOUSING

"We understand the frustration and strong emotions being expressed across our community," Kyle Kimball, the school's vice president for university relations, told Fox News in a statement. "Those concerns deserve to be heard, but damaging property is not the answer. We are investigating the vandalism at Day Hall and will address it in accordance with University policy and applicable law."
Tompkins County prosecutors declined to file criminal charges after Doe first reported the incident to university police in 2024.
FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS

Gov. Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James attend a press conference regarding an investigation into alleged sexual assault at Cornell University, in New York City, Oct. 2, 2026. (Reuters/Jeenah Moon)

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has said Doe's November 2024 sworn statement did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."
SEND US A TIP

However, according to a local CBS New York report, there is a transcript of what she later told investigators in a two-day interview on Nov. 14 and 15, where she distinguished an initial consensual encounter from allegations of assault that took place later at the party, reportedly telling them, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
"Nobody knows this information about the transcript and that gives me something to really dig into because that changes the landscape for me," Van Houten told the outlet.

A general view of Day Hall on the campus of  Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, Monday, October 5, 2026. The building was vandalized early Monday morning with graffiti which would suggest that the attack is in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024, accused are some members of the Chi Phi fraternity. (Varsha Bhargava / The Cornell Daily Sun)
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor last week to examine the allegations raised in Doe's lawsuit.

Jeremy Saland, the attorney for one of the former fraternity brothers named in the lawsuit, Scott Kretzschmar, told Fox News Digital that his client welcomes "a full and thorough investigation" into Doe's allegations.

"Fairness and justice demand it, and she deserves nothing less," Saland said. "Justice also requires that those entrusted with the investigation reach conclusions from the evidence, not from statements made before the evidence has been reviewed. Though Scott has never been accused of rape, he is confident that an objective and honest process will clear him of any criminal wrongdoing."

title: Shark bites fisherman twice during kayaking encounter along California beach
summary: A Malibu shark encounter sent a kayaker to the hospital after he reportedly reeled in a suspected mako shark while fishing off the California coast.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A kayaker fishing off a Malibu beach was rushed to a local hospital Sunday morning after a shark encounter reportedly left him with two bite wounds.
The incident occurred near Paradise Cove in Los Angeles County, according to KTLA.
Witnesses told the outlet that the fisherman had reeled in what was believed to be a mako shark and was attempting to release it when the animal bit him, causing him to fall into the water.

The shark then bit him a second time before swimming away, according to reports. The Los Angeles County Fire Department initially described the incident as a shark attack but later characterized it as a "fishing accident," ABC 7 reported.
SWIMMER RUSHED TO HOSPITAL AFTER SUSPECTED SHARK ATTACK AT MARTHA’S VINEYARD

A person paddles a fishing kayak in San Francisco Bay on April 1, 2017. A fisherman kayaking off Malibu was reportedly bitten twice by a shark on Oct. 4, 2026. (MediaNews Group/Bay Area News via Getty Images)
A manager at the nearby Paradise Cove Beach Cafe said he saw the victim's injuries near his legs.
"He was bitten in two places," the manager told KTLA. "I saw there were some teeth marks on his lower leg and above the knee."
AUSTRALIAN SURFER RISKED HIS LIFE TO SAVE FELLOW SURFER WHO HAD BEEN ATTACKED BY A SHARK
Video captured a lifeguard rushing toward the fisherman moments after the attack, while a small fishing boat floated nearby.
A fisherman reportedly rushed to the victim’s aid, pulled him from the water onto his boat and brought the fisherman back to shore, KTLA said.
A view of the Malibu Pier in Malibu, California, on Aug. 21, 2026. A shark encounter off a Malibu beach sent an injured fisherman to a local hospital. (Apu Gomes/Getty Images)
The victim reportedly called his girlfriend, a retired lifeguard, who helped him from the boat, assisted him onshore and called for emergency responders.
Los Angeles County Fire Department crews responded to the scene and took the victim to a local hospital, the outlet said.
Recalling the incident, the cafe manager reportedly said, "We’ve had a lot of crazy stuff happen here, but we’ve never had a shark attack like that."
The beach remained open following the incident, ABC 7 reported.
A Shortfin Mako Shark swims under the surface in open water. (Nano Calvo/VWPics/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Chances of encountering a shark in Southern California are higher in October, when warmer coastal waters attract both prey and juvenile sharks. Female sharks often use shallow, warmer waters as nursery grounds, where young sharks can feed and grow with relative protection.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Los Angeles County Fire Department for more information.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Mass shooting at Georgia block party leaves 2 dead, 35 injured
summary: A mass shooting at a block party in South Georgia left two people dead and more than three dozen others wounded early Sunday morning, according to officials.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A mass shooting at a neighborhood block party in South Georgia left two people dead and dozens wounded early Sunday morning, according to officials.
More than 1,000 people were gathered as more than 50 shots were fired in at least two locations about a block apart in Vienna, Georgia, according to Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy.

Deputies were on patrol at a neighborhood block party around 1:25 a.m. when shots were fired on the 900 block of Pine Street, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation said in a statement. The sheriff's office had requested the assistance of the GBI.

Two people were pronounced dead at the scene from gunshot wounds. Most of the 35 injured victims suffered gunshot wounds, while several others were hit by cars or suffered other injuries as people fled the scene. The 35 injured victims were transported to hospitals for treatment.
LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY PARK SHOOTING KILLS 1, INJURES 4 DURING LIVE BAND PERFORMANCE
Authorities investigate the scene of a mass shooting where at least two people died and 35 were injured on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026, in Vienna, Georgia. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)
Peavy said people were "going every direction" and, even as officers were on the scene, more gunfire erupted about a block away.
"We don’t know if it’s coming at us or someone else," he said at a press conference on Sunday. "You just have to keep doing what you’re doing and hope you don’t get hit by gunfire."
The GBI said the ages of the injured victims range from 14 to 51 and their conditions range from stable to critical.
The victims killed in the shooting were identified as Jaquevion Jackson, 21, of Cordele, and Macaleb Jackson, 23, of Hawkinsville, the agency said.
The incident happened over homecoming weekend for Dooly County High School.
SHOOTING NEAR BALTIMORE YOUTH FOOTBALL EVENT LEAVES 12-YEAR-OLD GIRL DEAD, 3 ADULTS WOUNDED
The victims who were killed in this shooting were identified as 21-year-old Jaquevion Jackson, of Cordele, and 23-year-old Macaleb Jackson, of Hawkinsville. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)
The superintendent of the Dooly County School System, Sherrod Willaford, said the shooting was not at a school-sponsored event.
"We recognize that its impact may reach many of our students, families, and staff," he said in a statement.
Schools will open on Monday, but additional safety measures have been implemented.
Vienna Mayor Eddie Daniels said the city had not issued any kind of permit for the block party, and he did not know if it was a homecoming party.
The ages of the injured victims range from 14 to 51 and their conditions range from stable to critical. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Authorities have not arrested any suspects, identified a potential motive or said how many shooters may have been involved.
"Please turn yourself in, because we're doing everything we can to find out who you are," Peavy said.
The incident remains under investigation.

Vienna is about 130 miles south of Atlanta and about a 50-mile drive south on the Interstate 75 corridor from Macon, where 12 teenagers were wounded by gunfire during a confrontation at a birthday party last week at a city park.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Attorney for accused Cornell student calls on Letitia James to step aside over prior comments
summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James faces a recusal call after her prior public statements appeared to support the accuser in the Cornell alleged sexual assault case.
story: Criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno discusses backlash against New York Attorney General Letitia James over her comments on the alleged 2024 Cornell University gang rape case on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’

New York Attorney General Letitia James is facing a call to step aside from the investigation into the alleged Cornell sexual assault after an attorney for one of the accused students questioned whether she had publicly accepted the allegations before taking over the case.

Andrew Miltenberg, who represents one of seven former fraternity members accused in a civil lawsuit, said James’ earlier statements supporting the accuser created an "avoidable question about the appearance of impartiality."
"The concern is whether the public can have confidence that the investigation begins without any predetermined view of the facts," Miltenberg said in a statement to Fox News.
AOC'S DRAMATIC RETELLING OF CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS COLLIDES WITH COMPLAINT DETAILS

New York Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James attend a press conference in New York City on October 2, 2026, regarding an investigation into alleged sexual assault at Cornell University. (REUTERS/Jeenah Moon)

Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed the attorney general’s office as special prosecutor Thursday, replacing Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten in the investigation into an alleged October 2024 sexual assault at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house.

The woman, identified in court papers as Jane Doe, alleges seven former fraternity members drugged and sexually assaulted her. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.
DELETED EMAIL DETAILS ALLEGED TRUMP-TARGETING PUSH INSIDE LETITIA JAMES’ OFFICE: ‘FIND AND PURSUE CRIMES’
The civil lawsuit alleges Jane Doe was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven former Cornell fraternity members at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. (TW Farlow/Getty Images)

Miltenberg’s objection centers on comments James made before her office was appointed to lead the criminal investigation. She publicly described what the woman had "been forced to endure" as "horrific and unacceptable" and told her, together with "all survivors," that "we stand with you."
When asked at Friday’s news conference about her objectivity in light of the Facebook post, James said, "I will not comment on a Facebook post."
Criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor Donna Rotunno also questioned James’ role during an appearance on Fox News’ "The Big Weekend Show."
"But it should be fair. It should be impartial. And it should not be from someone who’s already made a public statement on Facebook about it," Rotunno said of reopening the investigation.
James has said the investigation will be guided by "the facts and the law."
Miltenberg said his concerns were not political and did not diminish the seriousness of sexual assault allegations.
TRUMP LAWYERS TARGET WHAT LETITIA JAMES WON’T SAY ABOUT EVIDENCE IN $450M CASE

An attorney for one of the accused students argues James should personally step aside because she publicly expressed support for the accuser before being appointed special prosecutor, creating what he says is an appearance-of-impartiality problem. (Matt Burkhartt/Getty Images)

"There is nothing improper about expressing compassion for someone who reports a sexual assault," he said. "But there is an important difference between supporting a person who makes an allegation and appearing to accept the factual premise of that allegation before conducting an investigation."
He urged James to personally recuse herself while allowing senior prosecutors in her office who have not publicly commented on the merits of the allegations to handle the investigation.
"That would not weaken the investigation. It would strengthen it," Miltenberg said.
He argued that the same concerns about independence and public confidence that prompted the appointment of a special prosecutor should apply to the person leading the replacement investigation.
LETITIA JAMES’ RE-ELECTION CUSHION SHRINKS AS LITTLE-KNOWN CHALLENGER STARTS TURNING HEADS

New York Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James attend a press conference regarding an investigation into alleged sexual assault at Cornell University, in New York City, October 2, 2026. (REUTERS/Jeenah Moon)
"I am not suggesting that Attorney General James does not believe she can be fair," he said.

The case drew renewed scrutiny after Doe filed a civil lawsuit Sept. 16, nearly two years after the alleged assault. The complaint also names Cornell, fraternity entities, Doe’s sorority and a local bar, among others, alleging failures to protect her.
BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE HANDS LETITIA JAMES SETBACK IN LATEST TRUMP LEGAL CLASH

Van Houten initially declined to pursue criminal charges, saying the signed statement his office received from Cornell University Police did not establish a crime under New York law. He said prosecutors assumed Doe’s account was true and that her credibility was "never in question."
He later reopened the investigation after the lawsuit surfaced.
CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS
Questions about the original investigation intensified when CBS News presented Van Houten with a fuller transcript of Doe’s police interviews that he said his office had never received.
"That wasn’t information that I had," Van Houten said, adding that its existence "changes the landscape for me."
Rotunno also questioned why prosecutors had not sought the complete investigative record before deciding against charges.
"The real question is, why didn’t the DA ask for every piece of information that the campus police gathered?" she said on "The Big Weekend Show."
She warned against allowing public reaction to drive the case.
"We are watching the court of public opinion take over here when we don’t know the facts," Rotunno said.

Cornell has separately agreed to an independent review of its handling of the allegations. University President Michael Kotlikoff said its disciplinary process resulted in two expulsions and two suspensions of at least two semesters. One student graduated before discipline could be imposed, and two were found not responsible for sexual misconduct.
Those proceedings are separate from the criminal investigation.

Cornell previously told Fox News it "fully support[s] the appointment of a special prosecutor" and is committed to "an independent external review of all aspects of how Cornell has handled this case."
Miltenberg said any decision about criminal charges should come from prosecutors whose impartiality the public can trust.

"The simplest way to remove that question is for her personally to recuse herself and allow an uncommitted prosecutor within her office to lead the investigation," he said.

title: California realtor nabbed at LAX in alleged China spy case targeting Taiwan president’s relative
summary: FBI agents caught Wanying Zhang at LAX before she boarded a flight to China, accused of secretly surveilling a relative of Taiwanese President Ching-Te Lai.
story: Central District of California U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli criticizes Democratic senators for blocking a fraud bill and discusses the recent arrest of a man for allegedly spying on behalf of China on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’
A California realtor accused of spying on a Taiwanese official’s family for Beijing was arrested at LAX as she tried to leave for China, federal authorities announced Sunday.

Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine, also known as "Heather," allegedly worked with an associate to photograph and record the family outside their Seattle-area home, according to a criminal complaint obtained by Fox News Digital.
"We just arrested a Chinese foreign agent at LAX attempting to depart for China," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli wrote on X.
CHINESE SPY INFILTRATION: MAYOR’S BUST ADDS TO GROWING TIMELINE OF FOREIGN INFLUENCE CREEPING INTO US

Wanying "Heather" Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, was arrested at LAX on Oct. 4, 2026, on a charge of acting as an unregistered agent of China. (United States Attorney’s Office - Central District of California)
Essayli said FBI Los Angeles agents arrested Zhang on a federal charge of acting as an unregistered agent of the People’s Republic of China.
She allegedly traveled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and sent them photos, videos and license plate information.
FEDS SAY US CITIZEN GATHERED INFORMATION ON AMERICAN TARGETS FOR CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY

"She coordinated the trip with an associate and used tradecraft to avoid detection," Essayli wrote. "She never notified the Attorney General she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense."
Speaking on "The Big Weekend Show" Sunday, Essayli said Zhang is a naturalized U.S. citizen and confirmed the alleged surveillance targeted a relative of Taiwan’s president.
"She was conducting surveillance on behalf of the Chinese government. She was acting as a foreign agent," Essayli said. "And she was spying on a relative of the president of Taiwan here in the U.S."
He said agents arrested her as she tried to board a flight to Shanghai.
FBI Director Kash Patel also issued a warning to foreign adversaries following Zhang’s arrest.
"Foreign adversaries take note: America is no longer a safe place to run your espionage operations," Patel said.
"Allegedly surveil a foreign leader’s family on U.S. soil for the PRC — and try to catch a flight back to Shanghai? Not happening."
"This FBI is hunting threats to our national security wherever they hide — and bringing them to justice," he added.
The alleged target was Ting-Yu Lai, the U.S.-based son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, CBS News reported, citing law enforcement sources. The complaint does not name him.
"Saw him. Young male. It’s that young one," Zhang allegedly messaged a Chinese government contact while outside the home.
"I am videorecording," she allegedly added before sending two license plate numbers.
CHINESE NATIONAL ARRESTED AT JFK AFTER ALLEGEDLY PHOTOGRAPHING US MILITARY AIRCRAFT AT NEBRASKA BASE
Zhang and her associate allegedly flew from Las Vegas to Seattle on Sept. 1, 2025, rented a black Nissan Rogue and waited near the family’s home.

When the target returned, a neighbor’s security camera captured the pair quickly sitting up and holding out what appeared to be phones to photograph or record the family, according to the affidavit. Family members, including children, arrived shortly afterward.
"While individual 1 took pictures, Zhang reclined her seat as if to avoid being seen," FBI Special Agent Kevin Holt wrote.
Days later, Zhang allegedly told her associate to transfer the surveillance photos through AirDrop.
BRONX MAN CONVICTED OF RUNNING SECRET CHINESE POLICE STATION IN MANHATTAN USED TO MONITOR DISSIDENTS
Wanying Zhang, right, appears beside a man whose face is redacted in a photo included in the federal complaint against her. (United States Attorney’s Office - Central District of California)
"Seattle pictures, don’t send via WeChat or text. Must be sent over the air. I have to send it back. He wants me to send it back today," she said in an audio message described in the affidavit.

Holt said he believed the instruction was intended to help avoid detection. The associate later told Zhang he had deleted the photos and cleared them from his deleted folder, which Holt described as an apparent attempt to destroy evidence.
CHINA’S INFLUENCE MACHINE: FEDERAL RECORDS EXPOSE BEIJING’S PUSH TO SWAY AMERICA
Investigators believe Zhang received the surveillance assignment during a June 2025 meeting with a Chinese government contact in Changsha, China.
"I can take care of this thing," she allegedly told the contact.
DEMS UNDER FIRE FOR ‘MALIGN CHINESE INFLUENCE’ AS SHOCKING SPY MAYOR DONATIONS UNCOVERED: ‘HOW MANY MORE?’
Holt warned that information about a senior Taiwanese official’s relatives, including their homes and cars, could give Beijing leverage over Taiwan’s president during a potential conflict.
"Engaging in surveillance of a close relative of a high-ranking member of Taiwan’s government is not normal diplomatic behavior, especially inside of the United States," he wrote.
Essayli warned on "The Big Weekend Show" that the threat extends beyond California.
"China’s very good at using people who are already here," he said. "I don’t think it’s unique to California. It is happening nationwide."
Essayli said Zhang is scheduled to appear Monday in federal court in Los Angeles and noted that defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The arrest comes months after former Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang was charged in a separate case with acting as an agent of China involving paid efforts to spread pro-Beijing propaganda in the United States.

Fox News Digital reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for comment and additional information.

title: US pulls all bombers from key UK base after suspected Iran-linked terror plot
summary: The Pentagon says its bomber force remains ready for global strikes after aircraft deployed to RAF Fairford returned to the United States.
story: Martha MacCallum and correspondent Stephanie Bennett report on United Kingdom counter-terrorism police charging a man with planning acts of terrorism, including against UK Reform leader Nigel Farage.

All U.S. Air Force bombers in the U.K. were returned to their home bases in the United States following a suspected terror plot that U.S. officials have suggested may be linked to Iran targeting a U.S. military facility last week, officials said.

About a dozen B-1 bombers were among the aircraft removed from Royal Air Force (RAF) Station Fairford in Gloucestershire, England, a U.S. official told Fox News. The base is the only European forward operating location for American heavy bombers.
"We can acknowledge now that all U.S. bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States," a department official said.
The Pentagon emphasized that despite the relocation, the bomber fleet remains fully prepared to launch long-range strike missions directly from the continental United States whenever needed.
FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT

A U.S. Air Force B-1 Lancer bomber is stationed at RAF Fairford in Fairford, England. The installation serves as a key European base for U.S. bomber operations. (Photo by JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

"The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities – including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States – anywhere, anytime," the official said.
RAF Fairford functions as a key European base for heavy American strategic bombers and has supported U.S. military operations, including missions targeting Iranian sites.
IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS
Police stand at a roadblock near RAF Fairford in Fairford, England, on Sept. 27, 2026, after authorities declared a major incident nearby. (Photo by Ben Birchall/PA Images via Getty Images)
Last Sunday, U.K. officials said three suspicious vehicles containing fuel accelerants were found near RAF Fairford.
"We can confirm that no improvised explosive devices were found. However, a quantity of petrol was recovered," officials said.
Authorities began investigating potential ties to Iranian state proxies and eventually arrested a British-Iranian dual national "on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio later said the suspected plot "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor."
President Donald Trump last week also told reporters that the incident may have been connected to Iran, which the United States has been at war with since February.

Ground crews prepare to load munitions onto a U.S. Air Force B-1 bomber at RAF Fairford in Fairford, England, on March 11, 2026. About a dozen B-1 bombers have been returned to their home stations in the United States. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A total of six people were arrested in connection with the incident, including five British nationals in their early 20s.
Police, however, said all the suspects have been released on bail, adding that the investigation remains ongoing.

"I understand why this development will have come as a surprise to many, but I’d like to reiterate that it was an investigative decision, and one which is grounded in experience and careful consideration of policing powers," officials said, referring to the release of the five British nationals.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Portland teen faces terrorism, attempted murder charges after school cafeteria chemical scare
summary: A 15-year-old Benson Polytechnic High School student faces 19 counts including domestic terrorism after allegedly mixing toxic chemicals in the cafeteria.
story: Multnomah County DA Nathan Vasquez demands school safety as he seeks an adult trial for a 15-year-old charged with attempted murder and domestic terrorism after a Portland school chemical incident. (Credit: Portland Police)

An Oregon high school cafeteria chemical scare that left a student in critical condition has escalated into a domestic terrorism and attempted murder case against the same teenager school staff rushed to save.

The 15-year-old Benson Polytechnic High School student faces 19 criminal counts after authorities said he brought chemicals from home and mixed them inside the Portland school Sept. 8, releasing toxic gases that endangered students and staff.
"Safety in our schools is not something that can be negotiated," Multnomah County District Attorney Nathan Vasquez said during an Oct. 2 news conference.
"That violence or the threat of violence in a school … it doesn't just stay in that building. It follows families home. It sits at the dinner table with them."
THREE SCHOOL SAFETY STEPS EVERY PARENT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE CLASSES BEGIN
Benson Polytechnic High School in Portland, Oregon, where authorities said a student mixed hazardous chemicals in the cafeteria Sept. 8, 2026. (Google Maps)

Investigators uncovered "concerning behaviors and statements" before the incident, including an interest in hazardous chemicals, explosives and violence, Portland Police Bureau Public Information Manager Mike Benner said.
MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY STASHING HOMEMADE GUNS FOR ROBBERY PLOT: SHERIFF
Portland authorities discuss attempted murder and domestic terrorism charges against a 15-year-old Benson Polytechnic High School student during an Oct. 2, 2026, news conference. (Portland Police)

The teenager, whose name has not been released because of his age, faces 10 counts of attempted aggravated murder, one count of attempted first-degree murder, one count of attempted second-degree murder, one count of first-degree domestic terrorism and one count of second-degree domestic terrorism.
Additional charges include unlawfully manufacturing and possessing a destructive device, possessing a weapon in a public building, unlawfully using a weapon and recklessly endangering another person.
15-YEAR-OLD ACCUSED OF FIRING INTO CROWD DURING DEADLY SEATTLE MASS SHOOTING CLAIMS SELF-DEFENSE
The teen’s lawyers denied the allegations and said he is receiving treatment at an inpatient mental health facility, The New York Times reported.
Vasquez said his office would seek to move the case from juvenile court to adult court, emphasizing the safety of the students and staff.
"And I want to be clear, they're teenagers, but these are children, and they deserve a safe environment," he said.
But the prosecutor sharply criticized what he called a broader failing of Oregon’s juvenile system, which ends its oversight at age 25 even if the person still poses a danger to the public.
A Portland teenager faces attempted murder and domestic terrorism charges following a chemical incident at Benson Polytechnic High School. (Multnomah County District Attorney's Office)
"I think that that is wrong," Vasquez said, arguing that the cutoff fails to account for the danger someone convicted of multiple killings or domestic terrorism could still present.
"I'm looking at conduct and how dangerous that is and what I consider to be safe for the community going forward," he said.
INJURED LOUISIANA BOY HAILED A 'SUPERHERO' FOR SEEKING HELP DURING DEADLY STABBING RAMPAGE
The chemical incident unfolded shortly before 8:30 a.m. while numerous students and staff were near the teenager, Assistant Chief of Investigations Franz Schoening said.
Teachers and administrators moved students away as the school nurse began treating the teen before first responders arrived. He was taken to a hospital in critical condition but survived.
SUBSTITUTE TEACHER ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRIGGERING FALSE ACTIVE SHOOTER ALERTS AT 5 SCHOOLS: SHERIFF
"Those first few moments were critical in preventing further harm and lives being lost," Schoening said.
More than 100 students and staff were assessed after evacuating, and at least seven required medical care following the incident, he said.
DETROIT-AREA COUPLE ACCUSED OF THROWING EXPLOSIVE DEVICE WITH ALARMING 2-WORD MESSAGE INTO NEIGHBOR'S YARD

An empty cafeteria is pictured in this illustrative image. A chemical incident at Benson Polytechnic High School in Portland led to attempted murder and domestic terrorism charges against a student. (Craig F. Walker/The Denver Post via Getty Images)
Sgt. Jim DeFrain, who supervises the investigation and the Metropolitan Explosive Disposal Unit, said initial testing indicated the presence of hydrogen sulfide, a toxic gas.
An Oregon National Guard team agreed with that assessment. Samples were sent to an FBI laboratory for further testing, with results still pending at the time of the briefing, DeFrain said.
The FBI was also examining electronic equipment seized during searches.
Vasquez said the investigation remained open and that anyone else found to have criminal involvement could face charges.

"If we determine or find any links, if there are people that can be charged, this office will charge them," he said.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Florida TikTok creator lands in jail after allegedly turning women’s private data into posts
summary: Florida TikTok creator Mark Stephen Asea allegedly exposed women's private data in over 100 videos after gaining unauthorized access to their devices.
story: Cybersecurity and privacy attorney Leeza Garber discusses how hackers used Meta's A.I. chatbot to breach prominent social media accounts on ‘Fox Report.’

A Florida TikTok creator who calls himself a "demonologist" and "Grey Hat Hacker" is back behind bars after allegedly exposing women’s private information online and boasting that he could track their movements through their phones.

Mark Stephen Asea, 36, of Port St. Lucie, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail Sept. 30 on a felony charge of offense against computer users. His bond was set at $35,000, according to sheriff’s office records.

The arrest revived a criminal case that had been closed months earlier. Asea was first arrested in April on stalking and computer-related allegations, but prosecutors dropped those charges in May before bringing a computer-access charge in September, court records show.
TIKTOK COUPLE CHARGED WITH ARSON AFTER HOUSE FIRE CAUSES $10K IN DAMAGE

Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail Sept. 30, 2026, on a charge of offense against computer users after prosecutors reopened his criminal case. (St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office)
The police affidavit describes two women who said their private information surfaced in Asea’s TikTok posts, including one who had trusted him to help with a computer problem.
In a video reviewed by a detective, Asea allegedly rattled off details about one woman’s devices and claimed to know her recent spending.
"Let’s talk about your actual password," he said, according to a transcript in the affidavit.
"How about we talk about the last 10 purchases you made online?"
The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat. Asea was not a member, she said, although she suspected he might have joined through a fake account.
Nobody in the chat had permission to share it outside the group, she told police. She also said she did not know how he would have obtained her phone identification number or banking information.
FBI INVESTIGATES AFTER SHINYHUNTERS HACKERS CLAIM THEFT OF AGENTS' PERSONAL DATA
Security experts warn exposed email addresses and phone numbers can fuel phishing and impersonation scams. (Annette Riedl/picture alliance via Getty Images)
For the second woman, the concerns began after what she described as a routine request for tech help.

She told police she allowed Asea to remotely access her computer in October 2025 to troubleshoot an application. Months later, she said, he claimed he had essentially placed a virus on the computer while she was in the bathroom, allowing him to view information without her knowledge.
She said she never authorized that access.
Then a photograph from a private Telegram message on her phone allegedly appeared in one of his TikTok posts.
Asea claimed in a comment that the image came from a WhatsApp exchange, according to the affidavit. But the woman provided investigators a screenshot showing the photograph in the Telegram message.
Police also documented statements in which Asea appeared to boast about finding her location through her phone.
TIKTOK IN LEGAL HOT SEAT AS STATE ACCUSES APP OF EXPOSING KIDS TO HARMFUL CONTENT WHILE MISLEADING PARENTS
Location tracking can reveal your routines and movements long after you close an app. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
"Thanks to the GPS within her phone, but what did I do?" he said in the video, according to the affidavit.

The alleged posts piled up. Investigators said Asea uploaded more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one woman, sometimes posting as many as six in a day. He also allegedly obtained a website where he posted a photograph of her getting a tattoo.
SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCER PLEADS GUILTY AFTER PRANK VIDEOS AT ARIZONA CHIPOTLE, OTHER BUSINESSES
The TikTok logo is seen displayed on a smartphone screen on July 3, 2026. (Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
His TikTok biography lists "Demonologist," "Clairsentient," "Empath," "PTSD," "Grey Hat Hacker" and "Woodsman."
The April affidavit documented a different account biography that included "former satanist" and "cybersecurity engineer."
Asea also faced a separate civil stalking protection case over the summer. A woman obtained a temporary injunction in July, but a judge dissolved it and dismissed that case Sept. 8.

Prosecutors reopened the criminal case Sept. 24 and filed the current charge alleging unauthorized access to a computer or electronic device. The records provided do not explain why the earlier charges were dropped or what prompted the renewed prosecution.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Months after the original charges were dropped, Asea is again facing a felony computer-access charge. He is scheduled to be arraigned Nov. 19.
Fox News Digital reached out to TikTok for comment.
